title: bug: under MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED=1, ps1 Find-MoeProtectedFile treats a PATH entry that reaches the project through an 8.3 short name, a subst or mapped drive, or a UNC spelling as outside it
description:
Planner input from CQ-RF07 (task-f3f364a6), finding 6, posted on task-2f22237b by worker-c9368191. The architect filed it separately because task-2f22237b's DoD covers only cmd.exe's cwd-first lookup.

Find-MoeProtectedFile (scripts/moe-agent.ps1, about :523-544 at 717c4019) skips in-project PATH entries by comparing Get-MoeRealPath strings: `$real.Equals($project)`, or `"$real$sep".StartsWith("$project$sep")`. That compares spellings, not file identity. So the same folder reached through an 8.3 short name, a subst drive or a `\\?\`/UNC spelling passes the containment check, and a node.exe (or agent CLI) there would be pinned. The function's own ponytail comment already admits the 8.3 case.

The JetBrains side matches by file identity (task-9a1da6f6, the volume serial plus the file index). This needs the user's own PATH to carry such an alias of the project, which is why it is LOW.

Fix direction: an identity compare (volume serial plus file index) of each PATH entry's real path against the project and its ancestors, or an explicit refusal of 8.3, subst and UNC entries under the marker, with a Windows ps1 row (node --test through Windows node.exe, or postflight.ps1). The sh twin compares inodes with `-ef` and is not affected.
definitionOfDone: Under MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED=1 on Windows, a PATH entry that names the project, or a folder under it, through an 8.3 short name, a subst drive or a UNC/\\?\ spelling is skipped by Find-MoeProtectedFile, so a node.exe or agent CLI planted there is never pinned. A row run through Windows node.exe proves it for at least the 8.3 and subst forms.
Legacy seats are unchanged; the protected-agent-command suite and parity-check.sh exit 0.

implementationPlan.description:
Implement the final-path compare in scripts/moe-agent.ps1. /mnt/d/moe-scratch/89579137-plan/proto-moe-agent.ps1.diff is the validated prototype (a reference, not the final bytes). Save with a tool-witnessed editor per the rail, keep the UTF-8 BOM and LF, then run the ParseFile check.
(a) Move Get-MoeSha256Hex with its 3-line comment, byte-identical, from above $script:MoeGateProcessDefinition (about :5358) to just above the '# A protected file resolves only from' comment (about :526). PowerShell defines a function only when its statement runs, and the type name below must exist before the first top-level Find-MoeProtectedFile call (the node pin, about :565).
(b) Add $script:MoeFinalPathDefinition, a C# static class MoeFinalPath. Its Of(path) calls CreateFileW with FILE_READ_ATTRIBUTES 0x80, share 7, OPEN_EXISTING 3 and FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS 0x02000000, and no FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT, so junctions, links and mount points are followed. It keeps the SafeFileHandle in a using, calls GetFinalPathNameByHandleW with flags 0 (FILE_NAME_NORMALIZED | VOLUME_NAME_DOS) into a 32768-char StringBuilder, and returns null when the open fails or the length is 0 or at least the capacity. Name it like MoeFrozenGateProcess: $script:MoeFinalPathTypeName = 'MoeFinalPath' + the first 12 hex of Get-MoeSha256Hex of the UTF-8 source, so a hot reload that reruns the file in the same process compiles a changed source under a new name. Get-MoeFinalPath($Path) compiles the type once (skipped when -as [type] resolves; Add-Type -ErrorAction Stop with the class name replaced) and returns Of($Path). Use C# 5 syntax only, because PS 5.1 compiles with the .NET Framework csc.
(c) In Find-MoeProtectedFile, keep the untrimmed real path ($projectFull = Get-MoeRealPath ..., with $project its TrimEnd): a drive-root project trimmed to 'C:' would open that drive's current directory. On Windows only, read $final = Get-MoeFinalPath $projectFull.
For error handling, a compile failure, a null final path or a \\?\UNC\ one writes one [WARN] line naming $projectFull and the reason, then returns $null. The line has no MOE_PROTECTED_ token and no new MOE_ code. Each caller then keeps its existing refusal: MOE_PROTECTED_INTERPRETER_NOT_FOUND, MOE_PROTECTED_AGENT_CLI_NOT_FOUND, or MOE_AGENT_GIT_GUARD_FAILED for the guard git. No proof means no trust.
Otherwise $projectKey = $final.TrimEnd('\') + '\'. In the entry loop, right after the existing string compare and only when $projectKey is set: $f = Get-MoeFinalPath $realFull (the untrimmed path, as the file join uses), then continue when $f is null, starts with '\\?\UNC\', or "$($f.TrimEnd('\'))\" starts with $projectKey under $cmp.
A network entry never counts as outside: a share or mapped drive can be rooted inside the project, and its final path stops at the share. This is the JetBrains rule in docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md, 'Protected profile: path is not a plain local Windows path'. POSIX pwsh keeps $projectKey null and today's compare; legacy seats never call Find-MoeProtectedFile.
(d) Rewrite the ponytail comment above Find-MoeProtectedFile to say this, and keep the file-level-link residual. No docs change: no doc states the old 8.3 gap, and the Protected control plane bullet already says outside the project.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: Under MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED=1 on Windows, Find-MoeProtectedFile compares each absolute PATH entry's final path (GetFinalPathNameByHandleW, normalized, DOS volume name) with the project's. A folder that is the project or under it is skipped however it is spelled: an 8.3 name, a subst drive (including one rooted inside the project), a \\?\ prefix, a junction or a mount point. A network entry, meaning UNC, an admin share or a mapped drive with a \\?\UNC\ final path, is never trusted, because a share can be rooted inside the project. A project whose final path cannot be read, or that is on a share, fails closed: one [WARN] line, then each caller's existing refusal. POSIX pwsh and legacy seats are unchanged.

A subst spelling of a trusted dir still resolves.
I2: a claude reachable only through a network spelling of a trusted dir is refused with MOE_PROTECTED_AGENT_CLI_NOT_FOUND.

Every existing protected-agent-command row, plus moe-call, agent-git-guard, prompt-cache-launcher and usage-launcher, stays green on the Linux and Windows legs. parity-check.sh and npm run lint exit 0.

scripts/moe-agent.ps1 keeps its UTF-8 BOM and LF line endings.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1) A volume-serial plus file-index identity of the entry and its lexical parents. Prototyped as proto-identity-walk.ps1.diff.rejected, it was green for six forms. But `subst L: <project>\bin` makes L:\ a root with no parent, so the walk never meets the project. JetBrains QA found the same hole (mem:gotcha-windows-subst-ancestor-walk). Rejected; it is the m4 mutant.
2) Refusing every 8.3, subst and UNC entry outright. It breaks legitimate subst PATH entries outside the project, and it still leaves the compare spelling-based. Rejected.
3) QueryDosDevice expansion plus an identity walk, which is the JetBrains fix. It needs more P/Invoke and separate UNC handling. GetFinalPathNameByHandleW canonicalizes every local alias in one call.
Chosen: compare final paths, and never trust a network entry. This mirrors the JetBrains rule documented in TROUBLESHOOTING.
planningNotes.risks:
- GetFinalPathNameByHandle can fail on unusual file systems (RAM disks, VeraCrypt, WinFsp, unmounted volumes). The entry is then skipped, which fails closed.
- Network PATH entries become untrusted under the marker. This is by design and documented in the comment.
- subst mappings are per logon session, so other seats see them for the row's ~15 s. substDrive only unmaps a letter it mapped.
- PS 5.1 Add-Type needs C# 5 syntax.
- In a double-quoted PowerShell string, `$name:` parses as a scope-qualified variable. Keep a colon from directly following a variable in the WARN text.
- Do not use an atomic temp+mv save for moe-agent.ps1. Use a tool-witnessed editor, then ParseFile.
